summary: Lightweight headless browser for AI agents, written in Rust, that fetches pages as Markdown and only renders pixels when asked.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Moli is an open-source headless browser built for AI agents. It runs real JavaScript, DOM, CSS, networking and storage, but skips layout and painting unless a task needs them, which keeps it fast and light. Agents can use it to fetch pages as Markdown or a compact semantic tree, take screenshots or PDFs on demand, and automate browsing through CDP, WebDriver Classic or WebDriver BiDi, so tools like Playwright can connect to it directly.
sixtySeconds.problem: Full browsers spend lots of CPU and memory rendering pages that an agent only needs to read. Moli works structure-first and renders only on demand.
whoFor: Teams running large web fetch or crawl jobs
Playwright users wanting a lighter browser
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it when your agent mostly reads and interacts with pages and you want lower resource use than a full Chromium.

overview: Install the prebuilt binary with the shell installer on Linux or macOS, or the PowerShell installer on Windows.
Run moli fetch to turn a page into Markdown or a semantic tree; add --layout for screenshots or PDFs.
Run moli serve to start an automation endpoint that speaks CDP and WebDriver. Licensed MIT or Apache-2.0.

features.title: On-demand rendering
features.body: Layout and paint only when needed.

limitations: Visual features must be switched on explicitly
Optional images, fonts and media are not fetched by default

steps.title: Give your agent the prompt
steps.body: Ask your AI agent to install the skills under github.com/lexmount/moli/tree/main/skills and follow them to install the latest prebuilt Moli binary, as the README's quick start shows.

steps.title: Connect Playwright
steps.body: chromium.connectOverCDP("http://127.0.0.1:9222") then use the page as usual.

tutorial.expected: Page content as Markdown, a screenshot, and a Playwright script driving Moli.

Add --resource or a specific flag such as --image or --font.
